name: Customer onboarding plan
summary: For every new customer, your customer success lead gets one plan for the first weeks: the result the customer must reach, the fewest milestones that get them there with an owner on each side, the promises both sides made, and each message as a draft. Nothing is sent until a person approves it.

sources.title: Fully Powered AI's own working guide for handing a working process to a customer: the first real use as the goal, steps a person can be seen doing, show then do then sign, the notes the customer keeps, the honest fix for each reason a customer stops in the first weeks, and a person who approves every message.

sources.contribution: Defining the moment a new user first gets real value before designing anything else, a short ordered list that starts with a quick first step, and deciding in advance what counts as a stalled user.
The three passes over the path to first value: list every step, take out each one the user does not need yet, then rebuild the path from what is left.

Sorting promises made in a conversation into those with a deadline, those without one and those that depend on the other party acting first, and counting only the organization's own promises as its commitments.

Checking each claim in a summary against its source and treating a claim the source does not support as unverified, for a person to settle, never as proof either way; here, a milestone status nobody reported.

The idea that people judge an experience largely by its high point and its ending, so the ending deserves design: here, the last onboarding session ends on the customer's own success, with something to keep and a date ahead, and no automated email stands in for it.

Judging how far a customer has set up by what they configured on purpose rather than defaults created for them, stopping the work and raising a risk when an account has gone silent, and naming a new pattern instead of forcing a case into an existing one.
